newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks post powerful advance to record close.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks post powerful advance to record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index charged to a record close on Tuesday, propelled amid heavy volume by a surge in banking shares and a continued bullish tone in the property sector.
The index rose 245.94 points to close at 13,485.33, after hitting an intra-day record high at 13,495.38.
"HongKong Bank and Hang Seng are leading the market," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities. "They contribute half of the index gain."
Turnover was a heavy HK$13.14 billion, the highest since January 5, 1994 when it hit HK$14.49 billion. Turnover on Monday was HK$10.55 billion.

The turnover "is impressively large," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading HG Asia. "People take advantage of the volume. When they see the volume it brings out the buyers, the sellers, the switchers, everybody," he said.
Shares in HSBC Holdings rose HK$5.00 to HK$163.00 and Hang Seng Bank jumped HK$4.25 to HK$95.50.
"The banks had been sold off for a week and the market was able to keep going on the investment property story so there is pretty healthy rotational buying around," said Lesko.
Analysts said Hysan Development's acquisition last week of a major Hong Kong property for a bumper price continued to buoy property counters.

Hysan rose HK$0.70 to HK$30.00, New World Development advanced HK$2.10 to HK$51.50 and Henderson Land rose HK$1.00 to HK$78.25. Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$1.00 to HK$96.50 and Cheung Kong added HK$0.50 to HK$69.50.

"Basically today it is sort of the same old thing with the property sector, but now the Dow has gone up 75 points as well," said Lesko. The Dow industrials closed at a record 6,547.79 points on Monday, up 76.03.

"It looks like institutional investors are really re-rating the market to a much higher level," said Edward Chan, research director at NAVA SC Securities. He said if other Southeast Asian markets did not show signs of recovery, Hong Kong would continue to benefit from a large flows of institutional funds.

Analyst said the APEC summit was also a contributing factor to the rise. "May be the positive feeling on the China/U.S. relationship as a result of the private meeting between (Chinese President) Jiang Zemin and (U.S. President Bill) Clinton is one of a lot of reasons Hong Kong is doing well," said Lesko.
